title: The Beauty in Civility the Cost of Immorality
body:
IUIC in the ClassRoom · 2025-12-13

Opens [Rev 12](/bible/revelation/12) · [Isa 60](/bible/isaiah/60) · [Isa 13](/bible/isaiah/13) · [Prov 29](/bible/proverbs/29) · [Eccl 12](/bible/ecclesiastes/12) · [Heb 13](/bible/hebrews/13) · [Lam 4](/bible/lamentations/4) · [Job 39](/bible/job/39) · [Isa 63](/bible/isaiah/63) · [1 Macc 2](/bible/1-maccabees/2) · [2 Macc 7](/bible/2-maccabees/7)
## Introduction *[[10:32](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QczbDHIehUU&t=632s)]* What our own immorality costs us, taught as part one of two: the cost first, the beauty of civility to follow. Years of sitting in judgments and counsellings put the pattern together, and the thread running through the whole lesson is that righteous anger is what gets sin out from among us, because the hell we are catching is our own doing and not the white man's. ## In The News - *[[1:40:22](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QczbDHIehUU&t=6022s)]* **A cat defending her kitten, first from a hawk and then from an owl that swooped while the kitten was alone** — That mother kept a circumspect eye for danger and got her baby out of the way; that is radical, and it is what our mothers and our women have to be - *[[2:16:22](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QczbDHIehUU&t=8182s)]* **Stokely Carmichael, Kwame Ture, on Dr. Martin Luther King's major assumption** — Nonviolence only works if your opponent has a conscience, and the clip as it was posted cut off the line that America has none - *[[2:32:35](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QczbDHIehUU&t=9155s)]* **A short on Boulder, Colorado, then Soldier Elisha of IUIC Memphis telling his own story** — Put in a school for the mentally handicapped because he was black, and his father forced by a sheriff with a shotgun to sign over his land, a wrecking yard, a trash company, a house and a restaurant, with black people coming against his father first - *[[2:36:32](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QczbDHIehUU&t=9392s)]* **A video on Rasheem Carter, the twenty-five-year-old from Mississippi whose skeletal remains were found a month later with his head separated from his body** — The police still call it an accident with nobody else involved; this is the cost of immorality, the kind of thing that happens to us because we broke God's laws - *[[2:39:31](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QczbDHIehUU&t=9571s)]* **An Emerge magazine article on the death of Emmett Till and his mother's forty-year agony, with the open-casket funeral photographs** — Mamie Till had the courage to show the world what they did to her son, and Tiffany Carter belongs in that same category - *[[2:42:48](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QczbDHIehUU&t=9768s)]* **Photographs of our own people in the streets, one of a girl shooting inside a car** — This is what comes of allowing families to be ripped apart by sin: nothing but hatred toward our own people - *[[2:44:32](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QczbDHIehUU&t=9872s)]* **A classroom video of a teacher singing the funny birthday song to a six-year-old boy, telling him he lives in the zoo and looks like a monkey** — Slide the cursor back and look at the black boy in the background who understood what he just heard; the rest of them are laughing and those two children are damaged forever - *[[2:47:23](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QczbDHIehUU&t=10043s)]* **Malcolm X on who taught you to hate the texture of your hair and the colour of your skin, and on the man worried about somebody in a bathtub who cannot swim** — Black people are the greatest hate group against themselves; we are out in the middle of the ocean with no raft worrying about a white man in a bathtub, and that is a sick way of thinking we have to take accountability for ## Scriptures Opened **[Revelation 12:12](/bible/revelation/12#v12)** *[[13:30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QczbDHIehUU&t=810s)]* > [12](/bible/revelation/12#v12) Therefore rejoice, ye heavens, and ye that dwell in them. Woe to the inhabiters of the earth and of the sea! for the devil is come down unto you, having great wrath, because he knoweth that he hath but a short time. - The devil here is Esau, the white man, and this class is not about him: he is only a tool in God's toolbox to put you in shape when you break God's laws, and he can go no further than God allows him. - We are God's children and the rest of the nations are bastards; when we will not deal right by the Father he takes the bastards and puts hell on us with them until we get some sense. - Woe to the inhabiters of the earth and of the sea is woe to all the nations, but the most fire comes down on the twelve tribes, because the pendulum of change in this earth is on our clock. - His short time is why the heat is coming harder than ever through TikTok, Facebook, the job, an old connection, a cousin, a parent: the one effort is to make sure you never wake up. - When a wicked thought comes, reason it out in your own spirit: am I going to entertain this evil, or walk away from it to stay on the path to the kingdom. **[Isaiah 60:2](/bible/isaiah/60#v2)** *[[19:25](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QczbDHIehUU&t=1165s)]* > [2](/bible/isaiah/60#v2) For, behold, the darkness shall cover the earth, and gross darkness the people: but the Lord shall arise upon thee, and his glory shall be seen upon thee. - Darkness translates into sin, evil and debauchery, and it covers the earth, meaning everybody is following Esau in his wickedness. - Gross darkness is on the people, and the people is us: the greatest level of complete evil, the most sin, is coming from the Israelites. - Money will not fix it. Give a people in that condition billions of dollars and we would be uncontrollable in evil; we are like wild weeds with no control right now. - The Lord arises on thee and his glory is seen on thee only when we get our minds right. **[Isaiah 13:3-5](/bible/isaiah/13#v3)** *[[28:04](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QczbDHIehUU&t=1684s)]* > [3](/bible/isaiah/13#v3) I have commanded my sanctified ones, I have also called my mighty ones for mine anger, even them that rejoice in my highness. > > [4](/bible/isaiah/13#v4) The noise of a multitude in the mountains, like as of a great people; a tumultuous noise of the kingdoms of nations gathered together: the Lord of hosts mustereth the host of the battle. > > [5](/bible/isaiah/13#v5) They come from a far country, from the end of heaven, even the Lord, and the weapons of his indignation, to destroy the whole land. - The sanctified ones are the men God cleaned up, and sanctification has to do something: go out and teach, wake our people up, break the bands and the bondage they are trapped under. - The mighty ones are the angels, called for mine anger to back the sanctified ones up, and they are with Christ in the spirit world sharpening swords. - He called them for his anger, because anger gets things done; when eight or nine heads get chopped off and you are the tenth one standing, you become an instant believer. - The noise of a multitude in the mountains is the governments in tumult over you waking up; the mountains are the governments, and every nation is watching us whatever they say. - They come from a far country, from the end of heaven, meaning the other side of the earth: God caused these nations to build the weapons of his indignation and he is coming with them to destroy the whole land. **[Isaiah 13:9](/bible/isaiah/13#v9)** *[[35:01](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QczbDHIehUU&t=2101s)]* > [9](/bible/isaiah/13#v9) Behold, the day of the Lord cometh, cruel both with wrath and fierce anger, to lay the land desolate: and he shall destroy the sinners thereof out of it. - The day of the Lord comes cruel, with wrath and with fierce anger, because fierce anger is what gets the job done; none of that soft waffle talk from the pulpits. - He shall destroy the sinners thereof out of it, and the sinners are the Israelites who refuse to keep God's commandments. - That is the ones still playing with adultery, fornication, crack, alcoholism and lying: the day is coming when they will be destroyed in Babylon the Great. **[Isaiah 13:19](/bible/isaiah/13#v19)** *[[37:32](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QczbDHIehUU&t=2252s)]* > [19](/bible/isaiah/13#v19) And Babylon, the glory of kingdoms, the beauty of the Chaldees’ excellency, shall be as when God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah. - Babylon the glory of kingdoms is the utopia sinning Israelites thought they were going to have with Esau in the sweet by and by. - They hold this place in higher esteem than the Bible, than the laws of God, than the commandments, than anything an Israelite says; they put their whole faith, body and soul into Babylon. - It goes down as Sodom and Gomorrah went down. The Babylon Isaiah and the prophets lived under never fell that way, so the Babylon they were prophesying of is this one. - It is destined to be burned with fire, which is the weapons Christ is coming with, and Revelation says she shall be utterly burned with fire. Precepts: - **[Genesis 19:24](/bible/genesis/19#v24)** > [24](/bible/genesis/19#v24) Then the Lord rained upon Sodom and upon Gomorrah brimstone and fire from the Lord out of heaven; Brimstone and fire from the Lord out of heaven: that is how Sodom and Gomorrah went, and that is how this Babylon goes. **[Proverbs 29:18](/bible/proverbs/29#v18)** *[[56:57](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QczbDHIehUU&t=3417s)]* > [18](/bible/proverbs/29#v18) Where there is no vision, the people perish: but he that keepeth the law, happy is he. - Where there is no vision the people perish, and that goes for the father, the mother and the individual: no goal in righteousness means no course, and you will be pulled in any direction. - Vision is what a father is supposed to give: guidance, instruction, the goads that keep you from veering off. - If your instincts are not clean and strong you will hesitate at the moment of truth and falter when the trial comes, because your direction is not sharp and focused. - He that keepeth the law, happy is he. The law is the mark; anybody asking you to do something that breaks the commandments is Satan, and you should know it off the rip. - People ought to be afraid to bring evil to you. If somebody is comfortable putting gossip or wickedness in your ear, check your own spirit and ask what they saw in you. **[Ecclesiastes 12:11](/bible/ecclesiastes/12#v11)** *[[1:04:31](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QczbDHIehUU&t=3871s)]* > [11](/bible/ecclesiastes/12#v11) The words of the wise are as goads, and as nails fastened by the masters of assemblies, which are given from one shepherd. - A goad is a pointed rod used to urge on an animal, something that pricks, something that pains as if by pricking a thorn: a shepherd's stick that keeps the sheep in line so the wolves do not eat them. - The words of the wise are as goads: the words from your leadership prick your conscience and prick the sin in your mind to make you walk straight. - No pastor is supposed to be rubbing your back; the preacher is supposed to prick you with the words of God. - As nails fastened by the masters of assemblies is Christ coming down through the leadership, organising you and fastening you into a righteous assembly. - Which are given from one shepherd: the words are Christ's, not the leaders' own. **[Hebrews 13:7](/bible/hebrews/13#v7)** *[[1:12:13](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QczbDHIehUU&t=4333s)]* > [7](/bible/hebrews/13#v7) Remember them which have the rule over you, who have spoken unto you the word of God: whose faith follow, considering the end of their conversation. - Remember them which have the rule over you: respect them and pray for them, because it is hard work. - They have spoken unto you the word of God, which is the goads, the wise words that prick you. - Whose faith follow: the faith we believe in is with us and we are with that faith. - Considering the end of their conversation means you come among us to hear godly discourse on how to keep your life right, and the same is wanted of the conversations the sisters have among themselves. **[Hebrews 13:17](/bible/hebrews/13#v17)** *[[1:17:08](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QczbDHIehUU&t=4628s)]* > [17](/bible/hebrews/13#v17) Obey them that have the rule over you, and submit yourselves: for they watch for your souls, as they that must give account, that they may do it with joy, and not with grief: for that is unprofitable for you. - Obey them that have the rule over you and submit yourselves, because what they are giving you is the scriptures that prick you into righteousness. - Think about the near misses, sisters: where your lives would be, and the men who would have put another notch on a belt and walked away from you. - They watch for your souls as they that must give account: when a brother or a sister goes wrong, the first questions the leadership asks are of itself, did we go off, did we not handle that properly. - That is why a diligent inquiry goes all the way down: why you even thought about doing it, who was in the room, what time of day it was, so the behaviour can be tracked and the next one intercepted before they destroy themselves. - That they may do it with joy and not with grief: the account is given either way, and if it has to be given with grief it is unprofitable for you, not for the leadership. **[Lamentations 4:3](/bible/lamentations/4#v3)** *[[1:36:55](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QczbDHIehUU&t=5815s)]* > [3](/bible/lamentations/4#v3) Even the sea monsters draw out the breast, they give suck to their young ones: the daughter of my people is become cruel, like the ostriches in the wilderness. - Even the sea monsters draw out the breast and give suck to their young ones. - The daughter of my people is become cruel, and the daughter of my people is the Israelite women. - Cruel like the ostriches in the wilderness: we throw our babies down garbage disposals and abort them, and no sea monster has ever aborted its babies. **[Job 39:13-15](/bible/job/39#v13)** *[[1:38:44](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QczbDHIehUU&t=5924s)]* > [13](/bible/job/39#v13) Gavest thou the goodly wings unto the peacocks? or wings and feathers unto the ostrich? > > [14](/bible/job/39#v14) Which leaveth her eggs in the earth, and warmeth them in dust, > > [15](/bible/job/39#v15) And forgetteth that the foot may crush them, or that the wild beast may break them. - God gave the peacock goodly wings and gave the ostrich wings and feathers too. - She leaves her eggs in the earth and warms them in the dust, sitting on them hoping for them to hatch. - Then she forgetteth that the foot may crush them: she gets up and smashes the egg she just warmed. - That is the mentality the world wants our women in, and the question is where the radicalness is to stop it when the animals have better sense than we do. **[Isaiah 63:1-5](/bible/isaiah/63#v1)** *[[1:45:44](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QczbDHIehUU&t=6344s)]* > [1](/bible/isaiah/63#v1) Who is this that cometh from Edom, with dyed garments from Bozrah? this that is glorious in his apparel, travelling in the greatness of his strength? I that speak in righteousness, mighty to save. > > [2](/bible/isaiah/63#v2) Wherefore art thou red in thine apparel, and thy garments like him that treadeth in the winefat? > > [3](/bible/isaiah/63#v3) I have trodden the winepress alone; and of the people there was none with me: for I will tread them in mine anger, and trample them in my fury; and their blood shall be sprinkled upon my garments, and I will stain all my raiment. > > [4](/bible/isaiah/63#v4) For the day of vengeance is in mine heart, and the year of my redeemed is come. > > [5](/bible/isaiah/63#v5) And I looked, and there was none to help; and I wondered that there was none to uphold: therefore mine own arm brought salvation unto me; and my fury, it upheld me. - Isaiah is given a vision of what he sees when Christ comes back, and it is a question and a response: Isaiah asks who this is coming from Edom, and Christ answers it is I that speak in righteousness, mighty to save. - Bozrah was the capital of Edom, and the dyed garments are blood, so this is about the white folks; Isaiah 34 gives the same thing when the sword comes down upon Idumea. - The winepress is people's bodies, and he trod it alone: of the people there was none with him. - I will tread them in mine anger and trample them in my fury: the day of vengeance is in his heart and the year of his redeemed is come. - Mine own arm brought salvation unto me, and my fury, it upheld me. That is the point about anger: it is the fury that carries a man through the work, the way anger pushed Samson's jawbone through those ribs. - That is how men talk. It is war talk, and the sissified men are scared to talk like it. **[1 Maccabees 2:19-20](/bible/1-maccabees/2#v19)** *[[1:55:35](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QczbDHIehUU&t=6935s)]* > [19](/bible/1-maccabees/2#v19) Then Mattathias answered and spake with a loud voice, Though all the nations that are under the king’s dominion obey him, and fall away every one from the religion of their fathers, and give consent to his commandments: > > [20](/bible/1-maccabees/2#v20) Yet will I and my sons and my brethren walk in the covenant of our fathers. - Mattathias stood against what every nation under the king's dominion was doing, and it took anger to have that kind of resolve. - Yet will I and my sons and my brethren walk in the covenant of our fathers: one man against a whole government. - That is the mindset for a young girl with wicked boys in her ear and a boy with nastiness all around him in school: I do not care how many of you go to hell before I break these commandments. - Christianity tells you that you are not supposed to have that anger, and the minute somebody says something to you, you fold. **[2 Maccabees 7:27](/bible/2-maccabees/7#v27)** *[[1:57:57](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QczbDHIehUU&t=7077s)]* > [27](/bible/2-maccabees/7#v27) But she bowing herself toward him, laughing the cruel tyrant to scorn, spake in her country language on this manner; O my son, have pity upon me that bare thee nine months in my womb, and gave thee such three years, and nourished thee, and brought thee up unto this age, and endured the troubles of education. - She bowed herself toward him and laughed the cruel tyrant to scorn, right in his face, while the Greeks destroyed her sons. - It took anger for her to do that, and she lost all seven of her sons one by one and never consented. - That is how you women have to be, instead of letting somebody talk a hole in your head. **[1 Maccabees 2:21-26](/bible/1-maccabees/2#v21)** *[[1:58:44](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QczbDHIehUU&t=7124s)]* > [21](/bible/1-maccabees/2#v21) God forbid that we should forsake the law and the ordinances. > > [22](/bible/1-maccabees/2#v22) We will not hearken to the king’s words, to go from our religion, either on the right hand, or the left. > > [23](/bible/1-maccabees/2#v23) Now when he had left speaking these words, there came one of the Jews in the sight of all to sacrifice on the altar which was at Modin, according to the king’s commandment. > > [24](/bible/1-maccabees/2#v24) Which thing when Mattathias saw, he was inflamed with zeal, and his reins trembled, neither could he forbear to shew his anger according to judgment: wherefore he ran, and slew him upon the altar. > > [25](/bible/1-maccabees/2#v25) Also the king’s commissioner, who compelled men to sacrifice, he killed at that time, and the altar he pulled down. > > [26](/bible/1-maccabees/2#v26) Thus dealt he zealously for the law of God like as Phinees did unto Zambri the son of Salom. - God forbid that we should forsake the law and the ordinances: not bending at all, neither to the right hand nor to the left. - One of the Jews came in the sight of all to sacrifice on the altar at Modin, according to the king's commandment; people are supposed to be afraid to come before you with that, and he was not afraid at all. - Mattathias was inflamed with zeal, and zeal there is anger: his reins trembled and he could not forbear to shew his anger, and that anger is what gave him the strength to run and slay him upon the altar. - He killed the king's commissioner too, the one compelling men to sacrifice, and pulled the altar down. - Thus dealt he zealously for the law of God, so his anger was the result of keeping God's commandments. - Like as Phinees did unto Zambri: Phinees saw the sin going on with the women of Moab, and the Lord was pleased and did not destroy Israel because of that righteous anger. **[1 Maccabees 2:27-30](/bible/1-maccabees/2#v27)** *[[2:03:42](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QczbDHIehUU&t=7422s)]* > [27](/bible/1-maccabees/2#v27) And Mattathias cried throughout the city with a loud voice, saying, Whosoever is zealous of the law, and maintaineth the covenant, let him follow me. > > [28](/bible/1-maccabees/2#v28) So he and his sons fled into the mountains, and left all that ever they had in the city. > > [29](/bible/1-maccabees/2#v29) Then many that sought after justice and judgment went down into the wilderness, to dwell there: > > [30](/bible/1-maccabees/2#v30) Both they, and their children, and their wives; and their cattle; because afflictions increased sore upon them. - Whosoever is zealous of the law and maintaineth the covenant, let him follow me, and the rest go to hell: the same choice Moses put to Israel. - He and his sons fled into the mountains and left everything they had in the city. - Whole families got up and moved, children, wives and cattle, because afflictions increased sore upon them. **[1 Maccabees 2:31-35](/bible/1-maccabees/2#v31)** *[[2:04:31](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QczbDHIehUU&t=7471s)]* > [31](/bible/1-maccabees/2#v31) Now when it was told the king’s servants, and the host that was at Jerusalem, in the city of David, that certain men, who had broken the king’s commandment, were gone down into the secret places in the wilderness, > > [32](/bible/1-maccabees/2#v32) They pursued after them a great number, and having overtaken them, they camped against them, and made war against them on the sabbath day. > > [33](/bible/1-maccabees/2#v33) And they said unto them, Let that which ye have done hitherto suffice; come forth, and do according to the commandment of the king, and ye shall live. > > [34](/bible/1-maccabees/2#v34) But they said, We will not come forth, neither will we do the king’s commandment, to profane the sabbath day. > > [35](/bible/1-maccabees/2#v35) So then they gave them the battle with all speed. - It was told the king's servants that men who had broken the king's commandment were gone down into the secret places in the wilderness, so our own people told on us and were in a pact with the Greeks. - They made war against them on the sabbath day, which means they had studied us and knew we would not fight on that day. - Come forth and do according to the commandment of the king and ye shall live: follow Satan and we will let you live, and you pay for it in the end. - We will not come forth, neither will we do the king's commandment to profane the sabbath day, so they gave them the battle with all speed. **[1 Maccabees 2:36-38](/bible/1-maccabees/2#v36)** *[[2:07:38](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QczbDHIehUU&t=7658s)]* > [36](/bible/1-maccabees/2#v36) Howbeit they answered them not, neither cast they a stone at them, nor stopped the places where they lay hid; > > [37](/bible/1-maccabees/2#v37) But said, Let us die all in our innocency: heaven and earth will testify for us, that ye put us to death wrongfully. > > [38](/bible/1-maccabees/2#v38) So they rose up against them in battle on the sabbath, and they slew them, with their wives and children and their cattle, to the number of a thousand people. - They answered them not, neither cast they a stone, and did not even stop the places where they lay hid. - Let us die all in our innocency: they would have fought, but not on that day. This was keeping the sabbath commandment, not fear. - Heaven and earth will testify for us that ye put us to death wrongfully is a prayer for vengeance: God will judge you for what you did to his people. Christians do not think that way. - Christianity is a religion that teaches you to love everybody but your own self and to hate anything that upsets massa; where chattel slavery failed, Christianity perfected the slavery. - They rose up against them on the sabbath and slew them with their wives and children and their cattle, to the number of a thousand people. **[1 Maccabees 2:39-41](/bible/1-maccabees/2#v39)** *[[2:11:38](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QczbDHIehUU&t=7898s)]* > [39](/bible/1-maccabees/2#v39) Now when Mattathias and his friends understood hereof, they mourned for them right sore. > > [40](/bible/1-maccabees/2#v40) And one of them said to another, If we all do as our brethren have done, and fight not for our lives and laws against the heathen, they will now quickly root us out of the earth. > > [41](/bible/1-maccabees/2#v41) At that time therefore they decreed, saying, Whosoever shall come to make battle with us on the sabbath day, we will fight against him; neither will we die all, as our brethren that were murdered in the secret places. - Mattathias and his friends mourned for them right sore, because they were murdered. - If we fight not for our lives and laws against the heathen, they will now quickly root us out of the earth: at some point the anger has to kick in, because these people have no conscience. - That is what Stokely Carmichael said about Dr. King: suffering only moves an opponent who has a conscience to change his heart, and that assumption was wrong. - So they decreed that whosoever comes to make battle with us on the sabbath day, we will fight against him; neither will we die all, as our brethren that were murdered in the secret places. **[1 Maccabees 2:42-46](/bible/1-maccabees/2#v42)** *[[2:18:51](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QczbDHIehUU&t=8331s)]* > [42](/bible/1-maccabees/2#v42) Then came there unto him a company of Assideans who were mighty men of Israel, even all such as were voluntarily devoted unto the law. > > [43](/bible/1-maccabees/2#v43) Also all they that fled for persecution joined themselves unto them, and were a stay unto them. > > [44](/bible/1-maccabees/2#v44) So they joined their forces, and smote sinful men in their anger, and wicked men in their wrath: but the rest fled to the heathen for succour. > > [45](/bible/1-maccabees/2#v45) Then Mattathias and his friends went round about, and pulled down the altars: > > [46](/bible/1-maccabees/2#v46) And what children soever they found within the coast of Israel uncircumcised, those they circumcised valiantly. - The Assideans, mighty men of Israel voluntarily devoted unto the law, came to him, and all that fled for persecution joined themselves unto them and were a stay unto them. - They joined their forces and smote sinful men in their anger and wicked men in their wrath, and the rest fled to the heathen for succour because Mattathias and his sons were on the hunt. - That is what has to happen among us now, spiritually: wicked sinful people have to go, and it takes anger to make sure there is no love for sin going on in here. - They pulled down the altars and took the filth out, and the children they found uncircumcised they circumcised: you keep the laws or you do not live. - Saying all of this raises the bounty on your head, because in Babylon the Great nobody is supposed to teach you the truth; a prophet among the slaves who taught the Bible would be hunted and killed, like Nat Turner. Precepts: - **[Leviticus 5:1](/bible/leviticus/5#v1)** > [1](/bible/leviticus/5#v1) And if a soul sin, and hear the voice of swearing, and is a witness, whether he hath seen or known of it; if he do not utter it, then he shall bear his iniquity. If you hear it and do not utter it you bear the iniquity: that is why when you hear evil among us, you tell it. ## Class Questions - **Explain how the children are weighed in the balance when us parents do not deal right.** They emulate what they see and become the complete manifestation of filth; fornication and divorce leave a single-parent household, and a child who grows up with no father learns no value about himself, hates everybody who looks like him, and every fight he has is against his own self. What you see in the streets is fifty or sixty years of that. - **Where might their lives be had they not come through these doors?** Brothers and sisters who came in very young are captains and senior officers now, married, with children, jobs and careers, and they did not end up in drugs, whoremongering, debauchery, murder or crime; parents have come in afterwards and said these doors saved them from a life of destruction. - **Why do we have a problem with the word radical?** Radical comes from radius, a straight line from the centre to the circumference of a circle, and the circumference is as far as the centre point extends. So when they call you radical they are saying you are thinking beyond the mould they set for you to think in. Telling a man Christ is black, to pick up his pants and be a proper man is radical to them, and it is not criminal; it is what curbs the ugliness. ## In Closing *[[2:49:33](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QczbDHIehUU&t=10173s)]* What Malcolm is actually saying is take accountability for your sick way of thinking. We are afraid to stand up and correct our own sick thinking and to demand righteous thinking of ourselves, and that has little or nothing to do with white folks. Christianity is a major proponent of it, along with the school system and everything else in this lesson. So when are we going to be men, recognise how sick we are, and come out of that stupidity so that we can get to some civility, to a civilised type of living?
